Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of consistent findings: Four days of feeling unwell with sore throat, runny nose, dry cough, fatigue; initial fever that has largely resolved with acetaminophen/ibuprofen; exertional dyspnea but resting status comfortable; no chest pain; nasal discharge clear; exposure to a sick contact (colleague with sneezing)
- Likely diagnoses (from transcript and aligned DDx):
  - Viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza — High
  - Acute bronchitis (viral or post-viral) — Moderate
  - Streptococcal pharyngitis — Low to Moderate
  - Allergic rhinitis (as a possible contributor) — Low
- Notes on DDx vs transcript: No major conflicts identified; no conflicting elements require labeling as “conflict noted.”

Management Plan
- Rest and fluids; continue regular acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed
- Consider taking a couple of days off work; monitor for worsening symptoms
- If not better by next week, return for re-evaluation
- Red flags prompting sooner follow-up: high fever, increasing breathing difficulty, chest pain
- Additional tests or imaging: Not ordered or indicated in transcript

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute onset with sore throat, congestion, clear nasal discharge, dry cough, fatigue; initial fever responsive to NSAIDs/acetaminophen; exposure to sick contact
- Acute bronchitis (viral or post-viral)
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Cough developing after URI; dry cough and mild exertional dyspnea align with bronchitis after a viral illness
- Streptococcal pharyngitis (GASpharyngitis)
  - Likelihood: Low to Moderate
  - Justification: Odynophagia and history of fever; however concurrent nasal symptoms and absence of classic exam findings (exudates/adenopathy) reduce likelihood
- Allergic rhinitis (possible coexisting)
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Nasal congestion with clear discharge; systemic symptoms favor infection over allergy
